name: Maintenance Agents
description: The workspace's own maintenance crew, shipped as one installable unit: the System Analyst agent (daily architecture / silent-degradation / resilience / agent-run audit that opens a Kanban card per finding), the skill defining its contract, and the schedules that drive it — plus a cheap `aw-workspace-cli doctor` watch that only speaks up when something is actually degraded. Ported from the agentic-workspace monolith's aw-system-analyst skill, retargeted from SigNoz/awserv/Notion-by-curl onto the surfaces this workspace actually has.

skills.description: Daily maintenance audit of the aw-workspace install — silent degradation via `aw-workspace-cli doctor`, app health, architecture drift against the knowledge base, resilience gaps, and Agents Platform run failures. Three phases: revalidate open Kanban cards, scan and open a card per finding, publish the report.

agent_configs.name: Maintenance Agents
agent_configs.description: Read the workspace, reach the gateway. Full workspace filesystem access (the analyst audits that tree) plus the shared network, and the aw-gateway MCP server — without which there is no Kanban to file findings into and no knowledge base to check them against.

agents.name: System Analyst
agents.description: Audits the running workspace daily — silent degradation, architecture drift, resilience gaps, agent-run failures — and opens one Kanban card per finding. Reports; never repairs.
agents.capabilities: Reads the workspace's own health (doctor, apps, repos, skills, Agents Platform run history) and the knowledge base, turns what is broken into triaged Kanban cards routed to executor agents, and publishes a report. Read-only with respect to code and configuration.
use_cases: what is silently broken in this workspace right now
which installed apps are undocumented in the KB
why do runs for <agent> keep failing

tasks.name: System Analyst — daily audit
tasks.prompt:
/aw-system-analyst

Run the full daily audit as defined in the aw-system-analyst skill: Phase 1 saneamento of the cards you opened previously, Phase 2 scan across all four audits opening a card per P1/P2 finding as you find it, Phase 3 report. Start by loading the skill and searching the knowledge base — do not audit from memory.

tasks.name: Workspace doctor — degradation watch
tasks.prompt: `aw-workspace-cli doctor` just exited non-zero, which means a workspace component is degraded while very likely still reporting healthy everywhere else. Read the output above, identify which component is broken and what it takes with it, and say plainly whether this needs action now or can wait for the daily audit. Do not fix anything.

apps.reason: Provides the contributes.agents surface — it holds the Agents Platform base URL and identity token, which core does not. Non-required on purpose: an agent declaration that arrives before the provider is HELD and replayed the moment one appears, so this app installs cleanly either way and the skill is usable by hand in the meantime.

Provides the contributes.tasks surface — it owns the task tables and the cron tick. Non-required for the same reason as above: the declaration is held and replayed. Note the floor: seeding an 'agent_prompt' task needs the agent_slug forwarding added to register_contributed_task on 2026-08-13; an older tasks app seeds the row with a NULL agent_slug and it never dispatches.
Supplies the aw-kanban MCP server the analyst opens finding cards through. Non-required: without it the audit still runs and still reports, it just has nowhere to file cards — degraded, not broken.
Supplies search_knowledge_base/load_skill. Non-required, but the audit is materially worse without it: the KB is what stops the analyst from re-reporting findings that are already documented.
